subject: science
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF

topics.title: How scientists find out
outcomes: Learner can ask a testable question and make a prediction based on what they already know
misconceptions: Thinks science is a list of facts to memorise, not a way of finding out
hooks: Does curd set faster in a warm place?

topics.title: Observing, recording and fair tests
outcomes: Learner can record observations in a table and explain why only one thing is changed at a time in a fair test
misconceptions: Believes changing many things at once gives a quicker answer
hooks: Which cloth dries fastest on the clothesline?

topics.title: Grouping plants: herbs, shrubs, trees
outcomes: Learner can classify plants by stem, height and branching
misconceptions: Thinks all trees are tall and all herbs are small regardless of stem
hooks: Mint, rose and mango in your neighbourhood

topics.title: Leaf venation and root types
outcomes: Learner can link leaf venation (reticulate/parallel) to root type (tap/fibrous)
misconceptions: Believes all plants have the same kind of roots
hooks: Uproot a weed and a grass blade gently

topics.title: Plants and animals in different habitats
outcomes: Learner can explain how features of organisms suit their habitats (adaptations)
misconceptions: Thinks animals choose to change their bodies to fit a place
hooks: Camel in the Thar, yak in Ladakh

topics.title: Why diversity matters
outcomes: Learner can explain why conserving diversity is important
misconceptions: Believes losing one species does not affect others
hooks: Vultures disappearing in India and stray carcasses

chapters.title: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body

topics.title: Components of food
outcomes: Learner can name nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre, water) and their roles
misconceptions: Thinks only "costly" foods are nutritious
hooks: What does your breakfast give your body?

topics.title: Testing food for starch, fat and protein
outcomes: Learner can carry out simple tests for starch, fats and proteins and record results
misconceptions: Believes a food has only one nutrient
hooks: Iodine on a potato slice; oil patch test with groundnuts

topics.title: Balanced diet, millets and deficiency
outcomes: Learner can plan a balanced diet and explain deficiency diseases and the value of millets
misconceptions: Thinks eating more food always means better health
hooks: Ragi, jowar and bajra recipes from your region

topics.title: Food miles
outcomes: Learner can estimate how far food travels to reach their plate and why local food helps
misconceptions: Believes the source of food does not matter
hooks: Apples from Himachal vs bananas grown nearby

topics.title: Magnetic and non-magnetic materials
outcomes: Learner can test and sort materials as magnetic or non-magnetic
misconceptions: Thinks magnets attract all metals (including aluminium, copper and coins of all kinds)
hooks: Which kitchen things stick to a fridge magnet?

topics.title: Poles, attraction and repulsion
outcomes: Learner can locate magnetic poles and show that like poles repel and unlike attract
misconceptions: Believes a bigger magnet is always stronger
Thinks breaking a magnet gives a separate north and south piece
hooks: Iron filings around a bar magnet

topics.title: Finding directions with a magnet
outcomes: Learner can use a freely suspended magnet or compass to find directions
misconceptions: Believes the compass needle points to the North Pole because it is cold there
hooks: Make a needle compass in a bowl of water

topics.title: Standard units and measuring correctly
outcomes: Learner can measure lengths with a scale correctly (zero error, eye position) and use SI units
misconceptions: Starts measuring from the edge of the scale
Thinks 1 metre is the same as 1 foot
hooks: Measure a cricket pitch; why handspans don’t work for tailors

topics.title: Measuring curved lines
outcomes: Learner can measure curved lengths with a thread
misconceptions: Believes curved lines cannot be measured
hooks: Length of a river on a map using a thread

topics.title: Types of motion
outcomes: Learner can describe motion as linear, circular or oscillatory using a reference point
misconceptions: Thinks an object is either moving or not, without a reference point
hooks: A swing, a giant wheel and a train

topics.title: Properties of materials
outcomes: Learner can test properties like hardness, lustre, solubility, transparency and float-sink
misconceptions: Believes materials that look alike have the same properties
hooks: Compare steel, plastic and wooden spoons

topics.title: Grouping by properties
outcomes: Learner can group materials by properties and relate properties to uses
misconceptions: Thinks objects and materials are the same thing
hooks: Why are cooking pans metal but handles plastic?

topics.title: Hot, cold and temperature
outcomes: Learner can explain why touch is not reliable for hotness and use temperature in °C
misconceptions: Believes metals are colder than wood at room temperature because they feel colder
Thinks heat and temperature are the same thing
hooks: Put one hand in hot and one in cold water, then both in lukewarm

topics.title: Clinical and laboratory thermometers
outcomes: Learner can read clinical and laboratory thermometers safely and correctly
misconceptions: Thinks a clinical thermometer can measure boiling water
hooks: Check body temperature during fever

chapters.title: A Journey through States of Water

topics.title: Solid, liquid and gas states of water
outcomes: Learner can describe the three states of water and changes between them
misconceptions: Thinks bubbles in boiling water are air, not water vapour
hooks: Ice in a glass, water in a lota, steam from a pressure cooker

topics.title: Evaporation and condensation
outcomes: Learner can explain evaporation and condensation using everyday examples
misconceptions: Believes water droplets on a cold glass have leaked through the glass
Thinks evaporation happens only when water boils
hooks: Clothes drying on the line; dew on grass in winter

topics.title: Factors affecting evaporation and cooling
outcomes: Learner can test how temperature, wind and surface area affect evaporation and explain cooling by evaporation
misconceptions: Thinks a matka cools water because the clay is cold
hooks: Why water in a matka stays cool in summer

chapters.title: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life

topics.title: Handpicking, threshing, winnowing, sieving
outcomes: Learner can choose a suitable method to separate mixtures based on differences in size, weight and other properties
misconceptions: Believes any mixture can be separated by one method
hooks: Winnowing at harvest; picking stones from dal

topics.title: Sedimentation, decantation, filtration, evaporation
outcomes: Learner can separate insoluble solids from liquids and dissolved solids by evaporation
misconceptions: Thinks dissolved salt disappears and cannot be recovered
Believes filtration can remove salt from water
hooks: Tea leaves strained from chai; salt pans of Gujarat

topics.title: Characteristics of living things
outcomes: Learner can list features that distinguish living from non-living things (growth, respiration, response, reproduction)
misconceptions: Thinks anything that moves (a car, fire, a cloud) is alive
Believes plants and seeds are not alive
hooks: Is a seed alive? is a candle flame alive?

topics.title: Conditions for germination
outcomes: Learner can design a fair test for the conditions needed for seeds to germinate
misconceptions: Thinks seeds need soil and sunlight to germinate
hooks: Sprouting moong in a wet cloth

topics.title: Life cycles of plants and animals
outcomes: Learner can describe the life cycles of a plant, a mosquito and a frog
misconceptions: Believes tadpoles and frogs are different animals
hooks: Where do mosquitoes breed in a cooler after rain?

topics.title: Air, water, sunlight, soil and forests
outcomes: Learner can identify natural resources and their uses
misconceptions: Thinks air is not a resource because it is free
hooks: What do forests give the people of Odisha’s villages?

topics.title: Renewable and non-renewable resources
outcomes: Learner can classify resources as renewable or non-renewable and suggest ways to use them wisely
misconceptions: Believes water can never run out because it rains
hooks: Petrol vs solar for a car

topics.title: Stars and constellations
outcomes: Learner can identify bright stars and constellations and explain why stars appear to move
misconceptions: Thinks stars are tiny and close to the Earth
Believes stars disappear during the day
hooks: Find Saptarishi (Ursa Major) and Dhruva tara

topics.title: The solar system
outcomes: Learner can name planets in order and compare their sizes and distances
misconceptions: Believes the Moon gives off its own light
Thinks planets twinkle like stars
hooks: Chandrayaan-3 landing; spotting Venus as the evening star

topics.title: The Milky Way and the universe
outcomes: Learner can describe the Milky Way as a galaxy and our place in the universe
misconceptions: Thinks the Sun is the biggest star
hooks: The dark skies of Hanle, Ladakh
